 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle Cam Heyward has called for two major NFL rule changes after a series of controversial incidents, including the recent cancellation of multiple trades and a debate over overtime decisions. 
 Speaking on the Rich Eisen Show, Heyward was asked which rules he would change in the league. His first proposal was simple: teams should not be allowed to back out of trades once an agreement has been reached.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The veteran also wants the NFL to eliminate overtime ties, arguing that teams should have to keep playing or decide the result through a two-point conversion.
 Cam Heyward wants NFL to eliminate trade cancellations and overtime ties
 Heyward's first concern came after the Philadelphia Eagles and Cincinnati Bengals cancelled their agreement to trade Arnold Ebiketie. The deal was called off shortly after it was announced.
 "I think my first rule I would change is no trade-backs," Heyward said. "I've been seeing this a lot. I just saw the thing with Cincinnati and the Eagles. They cancelled the trade and there was a trade during the offseason between Baltimore and the Raiders that needs to be squashed as well. I think if you're going to make the trade, you make the trade. There's no way to get out of it."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement He believes both teams should be committed once a deal is agreed, rather than having the option to reverse their decision.
 "You're going to get in business, and you're going to get in the bed with them," he added.
 The second proposal concerns overtime, with Heyward particularly unhappy about the possibility of games ending in ties.
 "So, this is my other one. Because of the Browns game, right? And they go into overtime. I respect [Todd] Monken going for two. But I want the rule to be there are no ties ever in overtime. Either you go for the two-point play, or you keep playing," he said.
 Heyward added that he wants to see teams take more risks to win games, rather than settling for a draw.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement His comments came after Cleveland's 23-22 overtime defeat to the New Orleans Saints. The Browns had a chance to force a tie after Shedeur Sanders led them to a touchdown, but head coach Todd Monken opted for a two-point conversion instead.
 The decision attracted criticism, with former Browns wide receiver Jarvis Landry questioning the call on 4th and South.
 There has only been one tie in the NFL this season, between the New York Giants and Washington Commanders in Week 5. Heyward's proposals would remove the possibility of another, while also putting greater pressure on teams to honour agreed trades.
